title: Platform systems & services: dashboards, alerts, runbooks, roadmap, and team wiki
author: Aisha Kapoor
body:
Overview
--------
This document is the single-team reference for the Platform team’s systems and services: inventory, recommended how-tos, canonical dashboards and alerting rules, primary runbooks, quarterly roadmap items, and an annotated team wiki map. It is intended for platform engineers, SREs, on-call engineers, and engineering managers.

Scope
-----
- All platform-facing services owned by eng-platform (platform-api, platform-router, ingest-pipeline, metrics-collector, alert-manager, config-store).
- Dashboards published in the `Platform` Grafana folder and Alertmanager rules in the production alert group.
- Runbooks for P1/P2 incidents related to availability, latency, and data-plane regressions.
- Roadmap items that have operational impact (observability, autoscaling, runbook automation).

Systems & Services Inventory (short)
----------------------------------
- platform-api: REST/gRPC front-end for control-plane operations (owner: platform-api team). SLO: 99.95% availability; p95 latency < 120ms.
- platform-router: smart routing layer that selects execution pool; SLO: p95 selection latency < 30ms.
- ingest-pipeline: event ingestion & normalization; typical throughput 10k reqs/s during peak.
- metrics-collector: Prometheus-compatible exporter and pushgateway for ephemeral metrics.
- alert-manager: Alertmanager cluster routing to PagerDuty & Slack channels.
- config-store: Consul-backed configuration storage for runtime feature flags.

Canonical Dashboards
--------------------
Location: Grafana > Redwood > Platform
Recommended dashboard list (panel highlights):
- Platform Overview (owner: observability-team)
  - Key panels: RPS, error rate (%) by service, top 5 latency percentiles (p50/p95/p99), request distribution by region.
- API Health (platform-api)
  - Panels: 5xx rate, 4xx rate, avg request duration, concurrent connections, auth failures.
- Routing & Capacity (platform-router)
  - Panels: queue depth, routing latency histogram, pool saturation, fallback counts.
- Ingest Pipeline Throughput
  - Panels: events/sec, processing backlog, consumer lag, retry rate.
- Observability & Instrumentation Health
  - Panels: scrape success rate, exporter errors, metrics ingestion latency.

Dashboard panel naming conventions:
- Panels must start with service name (e.g., platform-api: p95 latency).
- Use Prometheus metrics when possible; prefer histogram_quantile for latencies.

Alerting (rules & thresholds)
----------------------------
Alert rules live in repo: infra/observability/alerts/platform/*.yaml (canonical CI job: alert-lint). Routing: Alertmanager -> Slack #oncall-platform -> PagerDuty escalation as defined per severity.
Primary alert tiers:
- Sev P1 (pagerduty): service_down, sustained_high_error_rate, p99_cpu_saturation.
  - Examples: platform-api:service_down when 3/3 health checks fail for 2 minutes.
  - Example rule (human-readable): "platform-api_total_errors / platform_api_requests > 0.02 for 2m" -> fires a high-error-rate alert.
- Sev P2 (slack + email, paged if escalation window crossed): latency_regression, degraded_throughput, config_sync_failures.
- Sev P3 (Slack only): elevated retry rate, increased 4xx traffic.

Recommended alert thresholds (starting point; tune per-svc):
- Error rate (5xx) > 2% sustained for 2m -> P1
- p95 latency > 250ms for platform-api for 5m -> P2
- Consumer lag > 5m -> P2
- Scrape success < 95% across exporters for 10m -> P2

Alert runflows and mute policy:
1. AlertManager groups related alerts and deduplicates; ensure alert labels include `team=platform` and `service=...`.
2. On-call triages in Slack; if P1, follow the P1 runbook and page via PagerDuty.
3. Use short-term mutes for noisy alerts only with owner approval and an explicit expiration (max 4 hours).

Runbooks (quick references)
--------------------------
1) P1: platform-api total outage
- Symptoms: 5xx > 50% or health checks failing 3/3 across primary region.
- Immediate steps:
  1. Acknowledge PagerDuty alert, set Slack bridge in #oncall-platform.
  2. Check Grafana: Platform Overview -> platform-api panels. Note pod/instance counts and recent deploys.
  3. Roll back recent canary or latest deploy if deploy_time < 30m: `kubectl rollout undo deployment/platform-api -n platform` (owner: platform-api).
  4. If not deploy related: check platform-router for backend pool health; run `kubectl describe` on failing pods and capture logs: `kubectl logs -l app=platform-api -n platform --since=15m`
  5. If configuration change suspected, revert config-store key `platform-api/config` to last-known-good via the management CLI: `platformctl config rollback platform-api --to-tag=stable`
  6. Notify customer-success if customer impact is expected > 15 mins.
  7. Post-incident: fill out incident postmortem template within 48 hours (link: /confluence/eng-platform/incident-postmortems).

2) P1: sustained high p99 latency (routing or backend slow)
- Symptoms: p99 latency > 1s and elevated queue depth.
- Immediate steps:
  1. Acknowledge and check Routing & Capacity dashboard. Identify whether a specific pool or region is affected.
  2. If a particular pool is overloaded, re-route traffic: update routing rule to fallback pool with `platformctl route update --service platform-api --policy=failover` (requires on-call with deploy privileges).
  3. Increase autoscaler target for the affected pool for short window: `kubectl scale deployment/platform-api --replicas=<N>` or trigger scale-up via cluster-autoscaler API.
  4. Investigate downstream dependencies (e.g., DB stalls, model-serving nodes). Open tickets and assign owners.

How-tos & Playbooks (common tasks)
----------------------------------
- How to add a dashboard:
  1. Create panels in Grafana under "Redwood / Platform" folder.
  2. Panel title convention: `<service>: <metric description>` (e.g., `platform-api: p95 latency`).
  3. Add annotations for deploys (use the CI deploy webhook).
  4. Submit a PR to infra/observability/dashboards with a JSON export and owner tag.
- How to add an alert rule:
  1. Implement rule in prometheus rules YAML under infra/observability/alerts/platform.
  2. Run `make alert-lint` locally and ensure CI passes.
  3. Open PR and ask for a reviewer from `@observability` and `@platform` teams.
- How to onboard a new service to platform monitoring:
  1. Instrument metrics (request counter, error counter, latency histogram, service_health).
  2. Add scrape_config in infra/observability/prometheus/scrape_configs.yml.
  3. Create dashboards and a minimal alert bundle (error rate, latency p95) and follow the PR process.

Retrospective (last major incident: 2025-11-18)
-----------------------------------------------
Summary:
- Incident: routing misconfiguration caused cross-region traffic surge and platform-api overload for ~42 minutes.
- Root cause: {human} incorrect routing rule pushed without canary; change landed during high-traffic window.
- What went well: Rapid rollback, effective use of runbooks, good customer communications.
- Action items (owner / due):
  - Enforce pre-deploy canary rule for routing changes (owner: platform-router / due: 2026-01-15).
  - Add deploy annotations visible on all dashboards (owner: observability / due: 2026-01-10).
  - Add automatic safeties to block routing changes that increase cross-region traffic > 15% (owner: platform-safety / due: 2026-03-01).

Quarterly Roadmap (operational priorities)
-----------------------------------------
Q1 2026:
- Improve observability sampling for long-tail requests (goal: increase p99 fidelity without high cardinality cost).
- Implement adaptive alert suppression during large-scale rollouts.
- Run cookbook exercise & game-day for platform oncall.
Q2 2026:
- Auto-remediation for common transient errors (scripted rollouts, controlled scale-ups).
- Migrate alert rules to unified rule templating system.

--------------------------------

- Runbooks: /confluence/eng-platform/platform-systems-services-runbooks-dashboards-roadmap-team-wiki-2026-q2 (this doc links to canonical runbooks).
- Dashboards & Alerts repo: infra/observability on GitHub (link in internal repo browser).

Ownership & Contacts
--------------------
- Observability lead: María López (marial@redwood.example.com)
- Platform oncall rotation: see team rota in team wiki (primary/secondary contacts listed).
- PagerDuty: service key: PRD_platform (don’t embed secret keys here).

Appendix: Common CLI commands & snippets
----------------------------------------
- Check health and recent errors:
  - `kubectl get pods -n platform -l app=platform-api`
  - `kubectl logs -l app=platform-api -n platform --since=10m`
- Rollback last deploy:
  - `kubectl rollout undo deployment/platform-api -n platform`
- Temporarily mute an alert group in Alertmanager (via UI): Select alert group -> Mute -> set expiration (max 4h).
